review_views.label: Anonymous native view
review_views.evidence: The native view shows an intact coast, river junction, islands, circular city, port, roads, fields, and eight separable highland bodies in one coherent plan view.
review_views.notes: Protected map geometry is crisp at native scale, but the highland interiors read as repeated nested contour rings and the lowest detached body reads as a rounded pill-like bar.

review_views.label: Anonymous full view at 25%
review_views.evidence: At 25%, the coast, river delta, central city, port, field grid, road network, and all eight highland silhouettes remain distinguishable without a crop or topology shift.
review_views.notes: Large-scale composition survives reduction well; fine paper texture and interior contour bands appropriately compress, while the detached low bar remains visibly capsule-like.

review_views.label: Anonymous full view at 50%
review_views.evidence: At 50%, the same shoreline, waterways, roads, settlement outlines, field boundaries, and eight highland bodies align with the native view while surface texture becomes more legible.
review_views.notes: Scale progression is stable and readable; the highland region remains flatter and more contour-driven than the richly stippled surrounding terrain.

review_views.label: Anonymous highland crop at 200%
review_views.evidence: The 200% crop resolves exactly eight non-touching brown bodies: two northern, two middle, three lower main bodies, and one detached horizontal body at the bottom.
review_views.notes: Every main body is dominated by nested closed contour bands rather than differentiated crest, spur, and saddle structure; the detached bottom body has a conspicuous pill-like silhouette.

review_views.label: Anonymous highland crop at 400%
review_views.evidence: The 400% crop preserves the 200% silhouettes exactly and reveals finer paper grain, antialiased edges, and additional separation between the nested interior bands.
review_views.notes: There is genuine 200%-to-400% information gain, but the added detail confirms field-wide contour substitution and confirms the isolated rounded bar rather than resolving it as an organic ridge.

review_views.label: Anonymous packet: overall composition
review_views.evidence: Across the three full-map views, the circular city anchors the composition, roads connect cleanly to the port and fields, waterways retain hierarchy, and the highland cluster occupies a stable northeast region.
review_views.notes: The overall map is coherent and legible, although the flat highland fill and repeated contour-ring treatment are stylistically weaker than the surrounding hand-textured terrain.

review_views.label: Anonymous packet: native-pixel integrity
review_views.evidence: Native inspection shows continuous coast and road edges, intact settlement linework, varied stipple, and no missing tile, straight image seam, luminous halo, or projection collapse.
review_views.notes: Pixel integrity is otherwise sound; the rejection arises from authored highland morphology, not from resampling, clipping, or broken protected geometry.

review_views.label: Anonymous packet: 25%/50% scale progression
review_views.evidence: The 25%, 50%, and native views retain identical coast, river, city, road, field, and highland placement while successively revealing finer texture and line separation.
review_views.notes: No parent-child drift or shared-projection collapse is visible; the same pill-like low body remains consistently identifiable at every useful scale.

review_views.label: Anonymous packet: 200%/400% highland information gain
review_views.evidence: Compared with 200%, the 400% view exposes finer base grain, clearer individual contour bands, edge antialiasing, and subtle tonal variation without changing any silhouette.
review_views.notes: The information-gain requirement passes, but the higher scale strengthens the evidence for contour substitution instead of revealing natural ridge anatomy.

review_views.label: Anonymous packet: immediate-failure sweep
review_views.evidence: The sweep found no side view, projection collapse, panel seam, white particle, hole, crater, root, river vein, fern, fishbone, dash bundle, or protected-geometry change; it did find a detached pill-like body and pervasive nested contour substitution.
review_views.notes: Two immediate failures are present: pill morphology and contour substitution. Either one independently prevents acceptance.

immediate_failures.evidence: Exactly eight separate highland bodies can be counted consistently in full50, highland200, and highland400: two north, two middle, three lower main bodies, and one detached low body.

immediate_failures.evidence: All highland bodies are presented from the same overhead plan view, and their silhouettes and spatial relationships remain unchanged from full25 through highland400.

immediate_failures.label: No panel seam or body halo
immediate_failures.evidence: No straight tile boundary, composited panel edge, or luminous outline appears through the highland bodies; the terrain-region boundary is organic and remains coincident across scales.

immediate_failures.label: No white particle, pill, hole, or crater
immediate_failures.evidence: A detached, long, rounded brown body at the bottom of both highland crops has a capsule/pill silhouette with smoothly rounded ends and little ridge articulation.

immediate_failures.label: No root, river-vein, fingerprint, or contour substitution
immediate_failures.evidence: At 200% and 400%, all main highland bodies are filled by repeated nested closed bands around local centers, reading as topographic contour rings rather than ridge anatomy.

immediate_failures.label: No fern, fishbone, dash bundle, or repetition artifact
immediate_failures.evidence: No branching fern or fishbone skeleton and no localized bundle of identical finite dashes is visible in the highland bodies or at their boundaries.

immediate_failures.evidence: The 400% crop visibly separates more contour bands and resolves finer paper grain, edge pixels, and low-contrast tonal variation than the 200% crop.

immediate_failures.label: No protected-geometry difference

scores.notes: Roads, terrain texture, boundaries, and protected geometry remain continuous; no straight tile seam, clipped insert edge, or body halo is visible.

scores.notes: Palette and parchment treatment are cohesive, but flat brown highland bodies filled with uniform contour rings are less organic and less texturally integrated than the surrounding stippled terrain.

scores.notes: Major silhouettes, roads, settlements, and fields remain clear and low-conflict for overlays; one point is withheld for the dense low-contrast nested bands inside the highlands.

summary: Rejected at 88/100. The anonymous packet is geometrically stable, scale-consistent, seam-free, and readable, but the highland crops show two immediate failures: repeated nested contour-ring substitution across the ridge bodies and a detached capsule-like low body that reads as a pill rather than an organic ridge system.
required_changes: Replace the nested closed contour-ring treatment with genuine overhead ridge anatomy, including differentiated crests, spurs, saddles, and falloff, while preserving the eight protected silhouettes and their positions.
Redesign the detached lowest horizontal body so it reads as an articulated organic ridge system rather than a rounded pill or capsule, without introducing particles, holes, or craters.
Recheck the revised 200% and 400% crops to confirm both immediate failures are absent while retaining the current scale information gain and protected geometry.
